description.short_caption: Erythematous, scaly lesion on the left elbow.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows a close-up view of the left elbow with an erythematous, scaly lesion. The lesion appears well-demarcated with a rough texture and prominent scaling. The surrounding skin shows some wrinkling and mild hyperpigmentation. No overt signs of ulceration, discharge, or crusting are visible.

Case_16006/figure12.jpg.source_caption: Slit skin direct smears of earlobes, Ziehl-Neelsen stain, with at least 1 bacillus in 10 microscopic fields (Bacterial Index: 2+)

description.short_caption: Ziehl-Neelsen stain showing acid-fast bacilli in slit skin smear of earlobe.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a microscopic view of a slit skin smear stained with Ziehl-Neelsen stain, highlighting acid-fast bacilli. A single bacillus is visible in the field, appearing as a bright pink rod against a pale background. The smear is consistent with a bacterial index of 2+, indicating the presence of at least one bacillus per 10 fields. The technique is commonly used for diagnosing mycobacterial infections, such as leprosy.
visible_findings: acid-fast bacillus visible as a bright pink rod
pale background with minimal cellular debris

Case_16006/figure10.jpg.source_caption: Skin biopsy with Fite-Faraco stain showing acid-fast bacilli.

description.short_caption: Fite-Faraco stain showing acid-fast bacilli in a skin biopsy.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a skin biopsy stained with the Fite-Faraco technique, which highlights acid-fast bacilli as bright pink to red rod-shaped organisms against a pale blue background. The bacilli are scattered within the tissue, consistent with an infectious process. The stain is specific for mycobacteria, aiding in the diagnosis of diseases such as leprosy.
visible_findings: acid-fast bacilli appearing as pink to red rods
pale blue background staining of tissue
scattered distribution of bacilli within the tissue

Case_16006/figure11.jpg.source_caption: Positive Immunohistochemical staining for S100 protein.

description.short_caption: Positive immunohistochemical staining for S100 protein.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a histological section stained with immunohistochemistry for S100 protein. The brown staining indicates areas of positive S100 protein expression, which is localized to specific cells within the tissue. The background is counterstained in blue, highlighting nuclei and providing contrast to the positive staining. The image demonstrates a cluster of cells with strong S100 positivity, suggesting the presence of S100-expressing cells, such as melanocytes or dendritic cells.
visible_findings: brown staining indicating S100 protein positivity
cluster of cells with strong S100 expression

description.short_caption: Erythematous lesion on the left knee.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a localized erythematous patch on the skin of the left knee. The lesion appears slightly raised and is surrounded by normal skin with visible hair growth. No signs of ulceration, scaling, or discharge are evident in this photograph. The lighting and focus emphasize the lesion's reddish discoloration.
visible_findings: surrounding normal skin with hair growth

description.short_caption: Erythematous lesion on the left leg with scaling and irregular borders.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows a patch of erythema on the left leg. The lesion has irregular, well-demarcated borders and is associated with mild scaling. The surrounding skin appears normal, and the lesion is located on a hairy area of the leg. The lighting highlights the texture and redness of the lesion.

Case_16006/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Skin biopsy, hematoxylin and eosin stain, with multifocal granulomatous infiltrate (4x).

description.short_caption: Skin biopsy with granulomatous infiltrate, hematoxylin and eosin stain (4x).
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of skin stained with hematoxylin and eosin at low magnification (4x). The epidermis appears intact, with a normal keratinized layer. The dermis contains multifocal granulomatous inflammation, characterized by clusters of epithelioid histiocytes and scattered lymphocytes. No necrosis or organisms are visible at this magnification.

description.short_caption: Hyperpigmented lesion on the right knee.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows a well-demarcated, hyperpigmented, slightly raised lesion on the right knee. The lesion appears to have a smooth surface with no visible ulceration or scaling. Surrounding skin is normal in appearance, with no signs of erythema or swelling. The image is taken at close range, focusing on the lesion.

description.short_caption: Erythematous lesion on the right leg.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a well-demarcated, erythematous, slightly raised lesion on the right leg. The lesion appears to have a shiny surface with no visible ulceration or exudate. Surrounding skin is covered with hair, and there is no apparent involvement of deeper structures. The lesion's appearance suggests inflammation or infection.

Case_16006/figure7.jpg.source_caption: Skin biopsy with H and E stain showing epithelioid histiocytes, giant multinucleated cells and interstitial edema (40x).

description.short_caption: H&E stain of skin biopsy showing epithelioid histiocytes, multinucleated giant cells, and interstitial edema.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained section of skin tissue at 40x magnification. The tissue contains clusters of epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated giant cells, indicative of granulomatous inflammation. There is also evidence of interstitial edema, with pale spaces between cells. The nuclei of the histiocytes are elongated and vesicular, and the giant cells exhibit multiple nuclei arranged peripherally or centrally.

Case_16006/figure9.jpg.source_caption: Skin biopsy with Ziehl - Neelsen stain and acid-fast bacilli.

description.short_caption: Ziehl-Neelsen stain showing acid-fast bacilli in a skin biopsy.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Ziehl-Neelsen stain of a skin biopsy. The background tissue is stained blue, while several slender, rod-shaped structures are stained bright pink, consistent with acid-fast bacilli. The staining highlights the presence of mycobacteria within the tissue, which are characteristic of certain infections such as leprosy or tuberculosis.

Case_16006/figure8.jpg.source_caption: Skin biopsy with H and E stain showing epithelioid histiocytes, giant multinucleated cells and interstitial edema (40x, oil).

description.short_caption: H&E stain showing epithelioid histiocytes, multinucleated giant cells, and interstitial edema (40x magnification).
description.detailed_description: This histopathological image, stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), shows a collection of epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated giant cells, characteristic of granulomatous inflammation. The surrounding tissue exhibits interstitial edema and a loose arrangement of collagen fibers. The magnification is approximately 40x, with oil immersion enhancing cellular detail. The findings suggest a granulomatous process, potentially infectious or non-infectious in etiology.
